metaDescription: Five genuine 30-quart air fryer ovens compared on heater control, racks, presets, footprint and cleanup for families that cook big batches.
expertTake: The Nuwave Bravo XL Pro with its adjustable top and bottom heaters is the best pick for cooks who like to tune the oven. The Our Place Wonder Oven Pro is the choice for a touchscreen and steam infusion. Skip the 30 quart class if you only cook for one or two, since these ovens take serious counter space.
introParagraphs: A 30 quart air fryer is really a countertop convection oven with a powerful fan, and it behaves more like a small wall oven than a basket machine. Racks, trays and a door replace the drawer, so you can cook a sheet-pan meal or a family-sized pizza in one go.

That size brings counter and power demands. These ovens are wide, deep and hot on the outside, and they draw serious current, so the buying decision is about fit, heater design and how much cooking you will actually hand over to them.

products.name: Nuwave Bravo XL Pro air fryer toaster oven
products.description:
Nuwave lets you change the ratio between the top and bottom heaters from zero to one hundred percent and pick among three fan speeds. That kind of control is unusual in a countertop oven and is the reason it earns the top slot for people who like to adjust results.

The oven also carries 112 easy-cook presets across twelve functions such as air fry, toast, grill and bake. Compared with the Our Place Wonder Oven Pro, it trades a touchscreen and steam for deeper manual control, which suits an experienced cook more than a casual one. Pizza fans can lean the heat toward the bottom, and bakers can lean it toward the top.

Ownership is about racks, trays and a hot, wide cabinet. Plan for several inches of clearance on every side and keep the oven off a shared strip. The big interior takes a real wipe-down after fatty cooks, so a drip tray and a regular scrub keep smoke down. Year-three wear shows up in the door hinge and the rack guides, which are worth a look when the oven is cool. A heavy loaded tray is awkward to slide into upper rack positions, so use the middle slot for the heaviest items. Weight on the door when open is also a risk, so never rest a hot tray on it.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want to tune heater ratio and fan speed for each dish.
pros: Three fan speeds for different foods
Suits pizza, baking and air frying
cons: Wide body needs generous counter space
Many options mean a learning curve

products.name: Nuwave Bravo XL Pro 2026 oven with grill
products.description:
The 2026 version of the Bravo XL Pro raises the preset count to 142 and advertises a redesigned fan and housing that Nuwave claims is much faster. It keeps twelve functions and a grill combination, so the feature set is broad.

The maker describes it as thirty-five percent crispier and several times faster, but those figures are marketing comparisons against unspecified baselines. A fair expectation is a strong convection oven that browns well with sensible loads. If you already like the older Bravo XL Pro, this is a refresh rather than a new design.

The large cavity wants a regular wipe and a clean tray, and the broader preset menu takes time to learn. Leave open space on every side while it runs, since a high-speed fan also moves a lot of hot air. Because it is a newer model, keep the receipt and register it early. If you cook two trays at once, swap their positions halfway through, since the fan side usually browns faster than the door side. The grill combination suits steaks and chops, but expect splatter on the roof of the cavity and wipe it before the next preheat. Compared with the older XL Pro, the practical difference is more about preset depth than about a new way of cooking.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want the latest Bravo with the largest preset list.
cons: Short track record as a newer model

products.name: Our Place Wonder Oven Pro 30 qt, 3 rack
products.description:
Our Place pairs a touchscreen with eight functions that include air fry, bake, roast, toast, broil, dehydrate, proof and reheat. Built-in steam infusion is the standout, because a touch of steam helps breads rise and keeps reheated food from drying out.

The heating elements are quartz and stainless steel, and the oven reaches 450F. Against the Nuwave Bravo XL Pro, you gain steam and a cleaner panel but lose the heater ratio control. It is aimed at buyers who value a good-looking, non-toxic-minded design over a long list of manual options.

The touchscreen keeps the interface tidy, and wet hands are the usual annoyance. Wipe the cavity after steam cooks to prevent mineral spotting, and use filtered water if your tap is hard. Allow room for the door swing and the hot exterior. Proofing dough at low heat is a practical bonus for bakers, since many kitchens run cold in winter. Treat the cooking time claims as relative to a conventional oven, and check food a few minutes early on the first few cooks. A silicone-tipped tool for rack handling saves your knuckles on every use.
products.bestFor: Bakers and everyday cooks who like a touchscreen and steam.
pros: Steam infusion helps bread and reheating
cons: No heater ratio control like the Nuwave
Steam cooking needs extra cavity wiping

products.name: Nuwave Bravo XL 30 qt smart oven with grill
products.description:
The original Bravo XL offers a 50F to 500F range in five-degree increments, with on-the-fly adjustment at any point in a cook. Its Linear T technology aims to hold the set temperature steadily, which suits baking and delicate cooks.

The wide range down to 50F gives it room for warming and gentle dehydrating, and the top end reaches 500F for hot finishing. Compared with the Bravo XL Pro models, it has simpler fan and heater features and a smaller preset story, but the core precision is similar. It is the older design in the family, so check which variant you are actually buying.

Upkeep centres on the interior, the racks and the drip tray. A countertop grill and griddle accessory is part of the pitch, so extra pieces mean more to store. Give the oven generous clearance and avoid power strips. Because it is the older line, check whether you are getting a current unit or a renewed one, since renewed stock sometimes appears under similar names. The Linear T claim is about holding the set temperature through the cook, which is helpful for custards and cakes that punish swings. Compared with the newer Pro units, expect fewer presets but the same fundamental convection approach.
products.bestFor: Cooks who prize wide temperature range and fine five-degree steps.
pros: Grill and griddle accessory idea adds range
cons: Older design with fewer fan options

products.name: NutriChef 32 qt air fryer oven with rotisserie
products.description:
NutriChef is the closest in size at thirty-two quarts, a little larger than the 30 quart class, so treat it as the near-size option. It adds twenty one-touch presets, a rotisserie and a Dual Cook mode in a family-sized body.

The rotisserie is the feature that separates it, since a spinning chicken browns more evenly than one on a tray. Dual Cook lets you stage two temperature steps in a single program. Compared with the Nuwave and Our Place ovens, the brand is less established, so check support and warranty details carefully.

Bigger cavity and extra hardware mean more cleaning, especially the spit and the forks. Dry them well and store them flat. Leave plenty of room around the oven for heat and the door swing. Truss the bird loosely so wings do not catch the spit rod or the element. Collect the drippings in the tray under the spit, since they are the main source of smoke if they burn. The spit hardware is bulky, so decide where it will live before you buy the oven.
products.bestFor: Families who roast whole chickens and want a rotisserie.
pros: Dual Cook stages two temperature steps
cons: Slightly larger than the 30 qt class
Less established brand and support path

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 30 quart air fryer is a convection oven, so you cook on racks and trays, not in a drawer. The Nuwave and Our Place models use doors and shelves, and the results depend on rack position. Buyers who expect basket-style crisping from a mound of fries in a big oven are often disappointed. Spread food on a perforated tray in a single layer. The fan sits at the back, so the rear of a tray often cooks faster than the front. Turning the tray halfway through is the simplest fix and the habit that separates good results from patchy ones.

The Nuwave Bravo XL Pro lets you set the top and bottom heater ratio and pick from three fan speeds. The Bravo XL focuses on temperature precision in five-degree steps. The Our Place keeps controls simpler. If you like to tune results, heater ratio is a rare and useful feature. A pizza wants strong bottom heat to set the crust, while a casserole wants top heat to brown the surface. A fixed-heater oven forces compromises that this control avoids. Fan speed matters too, since delicate pastry prefers a gentle breeze and a tray of wings prefers a strong one.

The Our Place Wonder Oven Pro adds steam infusion, which helps baking and reheating. The NutriChef adds a rotisserie spit for whole chickens. The Nuwave models skip both and rely on pure convection. Decide which extra you will use weekly before paying for it. Rotisserie hardware is one more thing to wash and store, and steam parts need descaling in hard-water areas. An extra you use twice a year is a poor reason to pay more or to give up counter room.

These are the largest countertop appliances in the air fryer family. Measure width, depth and the door swing, then add several inches of clearance for hot air. Under-cabinet placement is risky, since steam and heat rise. A dedicated outlet is also wise.

A large oven pulls a lot of current from a standard 15 amp circuit. Running it alongside a microwave or kettle can trip a breaker. Plug directly into a wall outlet and avoid extension cords. In older homes the kitchen outlets often share one breaker, so check which appliances live on it. If the oven trips the breaker on preheat, that is a circuit limit, not a defect.

A big interior collects splatter on the walls and heater. Racks, trays and a crumb tray come out for washing, and a regular wipe keeps smoke down. Steam models need drying to avoid mineral marks. Avoid abrasive pads on the cavity coating, and let the oven cool fully before cleaning. A weekly ten-minute wipe is far easier than a monthly scrub of baked-on grease.

howWeEvaluated.title: True 30 quart class
howWeEvaluated.description: We kept ovens listed at about 30 quarts and treated the 32 quart NutriChef as the near-size option. We left out 26 quart French door models and basket units. Capacity decides rack count and tray size.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat control
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared heater design, fan speeds and temperature steps. The Bravo XL Pro adjusts heater ratio, and the Bravo XL offers 5F steps. These are rare in this category.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras that earn their place
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed steam, rotisserie, grill and proof against actual daily use. Our Place adds steam and NutriChef adds a spit. Extras matter only if you will use them.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleanup and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted racks and trays and noted special cleaning needs. Steam models need drying and rotisserie hardware needs washing. Large ovens collect splatter on the walls.

howWeEvaluated.title: Footprint and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared size and features against each tier. Prices drift week to week, so we ranked tiers rather than quoting numbers. Counter fit often decides which model is realistic.

rows: Tune heat for pizza and bakes

cards.label: Nuwave
cards.text: The Bravo XL and XL Pro lines emphasise control: heater ratio, fan speeds and fine temperature steps. They reward cooks who like to tune a recipe.

cards.label: Our Place
cards.text: The Wonder Oven Pro emphasises ease: a touchscreen, steam and a tidy design. It is simpler to learn and better for baking.

howToChoose.note: Choose Nuwave for control and Our Place for ease and steam.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for rack space for two trays, strong convection and a door that opens clear of the counter. Confirm the circuit can handle the load.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Nuwave Bravo XL Pro is the best match for mixed trays. The NutriChef suits a family that roasts chicken often, and the Our Place suits a family that bakes.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want steam and a touchscreen, which points to the Our Place. You also gain from the newest Nuwave if preset depth and fan upgrades matter.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want strong convection with fewer extras. The Nuwave Bravo XL covers that need at a lower tier.

maintenance.why: Fat on the walls and heater causes smoke. Wipe with the oven cool and unplugged.
Baked-on residue is harder to remove later. Soak, then use a soft sponge.
Crumbs can scorch and smoke. A quick shake over the bin keeps the oven clean.
Minerals build up in steam systems. Filtered water and regular drying slow it.

maintenance.task: Check the door seal and cord
maintenance.why: A poor seal loses heat. A warm plug points to a bad connection.

faq.q: Is a 30 quart air fryer really an air fryer?
faq.a: It is an air fryer oven, meaning a convection oven with a strong fan. It crisps well on perforated trays but does not behave like a basket. Spread food in a single layer for best results.

faq.q: Can a 30 quart air fryer replace my oven?
faq.a: For many meals, yes. It handles sheet-pan dinners, pizza and baking for a family. A full-size oven is still needed for very large roasts and multiple pans.
The Our Place Wonder Oven Pro adds steam and proof functions, which suit bread. The Nuwave Bravo XL offers fine temperature steps for baking accuracy.

faq.q: How much counter space do I need?
faq.a: Expect a wide and deep appliance with a door that swings open. Measure the door swing and add several inches of clearance on every side. Avoid placing it under a cabinet.

faq.q: Do these ovens use a lot of power?
faq.a: Yes, they draw close to the limit of a standard circuit. Plug directly into a wall outlet and avoid running other heavy appliances on the same circuit.

faq.q: Is the 32 quart NutriChef too big?
faq.a: It is only slightly larger than the 30 quart class. The main difference is the extra counter space it needs. The rotisserie is the reason to consider it.
